overview.description: British variant of Whot, a Crazy Eights-style shedding game for two to six players. Use a Whot pack with five symbol suits and wild Whot cards; match suit or number on the play pile or draw from the stock. First to empty hand wins the round; penalty scoring over multiple rounds eliminates players who reach 100 points.
overview.deck: Whot deck (54 cards; British packs may have 53)

history.origins: Whot was invented and trademarked by William Henry Storey of Southend-on-Sea, England, in 1935; first marketed by Storey & Co of Croydon, later acquired by Waddingtons and popular in Britain in the 1950s–1960s. The British version described here uses a 54- or 53-card pack; the game also became the national card game of Nigeria with variant rules.
timeline: 1935: Whot trademarked by W.H. Storey in England; marketed by Storey & Co, later Waddingtons; popular in Britain in the 1950s–1960s.

nullReasons.evolution: British rules have remained stable; Nigerian variants added special card effects.
nullReasons.cultural: Strong cultural role in Nigeria as national card game; British play is casual and family-oriented.

setup.deck: A special Whot pack of 54 or 53 cards: five symbol suits (circle, triangle, cross, square, star) with uneven card counts per suit, plus four or five wild Whot cards (numbered 20). British packs from around 1990 often have four Whots (53 cards); earlier and Nigerian packs have five (54 cards).
setup.dealing: Dealer deals six cards to each player one at a time; remainder forms the draw pile. First dealer is chosen by cutting the pack (lowest card deals, Whot counting 20).

rules.objective: Be the first to get rid of all your cards; in multi-round play, avoid accumulating 100 or more penalty points.
rules.gameplay: Match suit or number with the top of the play pile, or play a Whot (wild) and name a suit. If you cannot or do not wish to play, draw one card from the stock; your turn then ends. First to empty hand wins the round.
keyRules: Play a card matching the previous card's suit or number, or any Whot card (then name a suit).
If unable or unwilling to play, draw one card from the stock; you may not play after drawing this turn.
When the stock is exhausted, shuffle all but the top card of the play pile to form a new stock.
Penalty scoring: circles, crosses, squares, triangles at face value; stars count double; Whot cards count 20. Players with 100 or more drop out; last remaining wins.

strategy.basic: Match when you can to avoid drawing; save Whot cards to change suit when the lead is awkward. In penalty play, prefer playing high-value cards (stars, Whot) early so they do not count against you if someone else wins.
tips: When the stock runs out, the play pile (except its top card) is shuffled to form a new stock.
Short game: one deal only, first to empty hand wins with no scoring.

nullReasons.intermediate: No distinct intermediate tier; British Whot strategy is mainly basic matching and when to draw.

play_card.description: Play one card onto the play pile: same suit or same number as the top card, or any Whot card (then name a suit for the next player).
play_card.constraints: Card must match the top card by suit or number, or be a Whot card. After a Whot, the next card must match the named suit or be Whot.

draw.description: Draw one card from the stock when unable or unwilling to play. Turn ends after drawing; you may not play a card this turn.
draw.constraints: Legal when the player has no playable card or chooses not to play. After drawing, the player may not play in the same turn.

engine.handRankingSystem: Penalty points only; cards left in hand are summed (stars double, Whot 20); no hand ranking for comparison.
engine.deckDescription: The British Whot deck has 54 or 55 cards: five pictorial suits (circles, crosses, stars, triangles, squares) with numeric values, plus special action cards such as Market, Pick Two, Pick Three, and Hold On that change turn order or force draws. No jokers in the standard pack.
engine.suitDescription: Whot uses five non-French suits: Circles, Crosses, Stars, Triangles, and Squares. Each suit has a subset of number cards; the fifth suit often has fewer cards. There are no court cards; special cards carry suit symbols but act as action cards.
engine.rankDescription: Cards show numeric ranks within each suit; the exact range varies by suit. Special cards have both a suit and an action (e.g. Market, Pick Two, Pick Three, Hold On, General Market). Rank order and special effects are defined by the British Whot rules.
engine.dealPattern: One card at a time to each player in turn until each has six cards.

notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Played cards go to a single face-up play pile; there is no separate discard action or pile.
